messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'greenridge-prod-pool' for tenant Greenridge Financial is reporting GPU capacity exhaustion. metric:gpu_queue_depth > 120 for 4m, 429 spike to 18% in last 5m. Paging on-call. Links: https://grafana.internal/r/d/pool/greenridge-prod-pool, runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-pool-exhaustion

sarah (on-call): saw the alert, I'm looking at queue and scheduler. Confirming customer impact: are we returning 429s or just increased latency?

lee (sre): 429s. Sampling from logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:23Z] tenant=greenridge request_id=xyz status=429 reason=queue_full queue_pos=142
[2026-03-15T10:12:27Z] tenant=greenridge request_id=abc status=200 latency=2.1s model=gptx-13b
```
Queue length climb matches spike in long-running streaming sessions.

anna (runtime): looks like a handful of pinned sessions holding KV cache and blocking eviction. Autoscaler isn't kicking in because pool is at hard max (config max_gpus=48). Their pool is single-tenant dedicated and bursting is currently disabled.

kevin (acct-eng): pinging Greenridge contact (eve) to confirm if they're running a migration or batch job. If this is unexpected we need to offer burst or move lower-priority work off. Eve?

eve (greenridge-liaison): hi — we have a scheduled overnight risk-analysis job that started earlier due to a timezone snafu, but ops says it should be short. We're seeing production latency from our product team. They're getting 429s on customer-facing endpoints. Sorry, that was our change.

beth (cs): CS is on standby, customers are opening support tickets. Need an ETA on mitigation before I send a status update.

jordan (platform): options, ranked: 1) enable emergency burst from shared pool (adds up to +12 A100s) 2) temporarily permit cross-tenant fallback to hosted variant (gptx-6b-quant) for best-effort requests 3) evict idle pinned sessions and reduce per-tenant concurrency to 4 4) ask customer to stop the batch job. Each has tradeoffs (latency, cost, QoS).

sarah (on-call): can we enable 1 quickly? What's required?

anna (runtime): enabling burst requires an approval flag and a force-scale command. I can run it but need product/ops approval for billing impact. Command: 
```
redwoodctl pools burst --pool greenridge-prod-pool --add-gpus 8 --reason "emergency support: queue exhaustion" --force
```
This will route new allocation requests to the shared burst capacity, expected infra cold-start ~60-90s. Existing queued jobs start draining as new workers come up.

lee (sre): if we do 8 GPUs we'll likely drop 429s under 2% in ~3m after nodes are ready. If Greenridge is okay with us covering emergency credit for today, we should do it.

kevin (acct-eng): I'll coordinate billing. Greenridge contracted reserved capacity is 24 GPUs; we can approve emergency burst on our account and invoice them later or apply their burst allowance. Eve, can you confirm if Greenridge will accept post-facto billing or prefer we use their burst credits?

eve (greenridge-liaison): they'll accept post-facto billing for emergency, please proceed — ops wants the job to finish.

beth (cs): ok I'm drafting a short customer-facing note: "We've detected transient GPU saturation for your dedicated pool. We are enabling emergency burst to restore throughput and will follow up with a detailed timeline." Will send once we're past initial mitigation.

jordan (platform): assignment: anna to trigger burst (now), lee to monitor queue and latency, sarah to own incident comms and handoff, kevin to own billing confirmation, beth to coordinate customer messaging.

anna (runtime): executing burst now. 
```
redwoodctl pools burst --pool greenridge-prod-pool --add-gpus 8 --reason "emergency: queue overflow" --force
```

incident-bot: Action logged: 'burst_requested' by anna at 3178882254, details:{"pool":"greenridge-prod-pool","add":8} (audit link: https://audit.internal/3178882254)

lee (sre): monitoring metrics... queue depth dropping from 138 -> 52 in last 90s, 429 rate down from 18% -> 4%. streaming latencies still a bit elevated.

sarah (on-call): good. Beth, you can send the short note now. Kevin, please confirm billing flow once you have Greenridge sign-off.

beth (cs): message sent to Greenridge ops and product leads: "We are enabling emergency capacity to restore production throughput. We'll update in 15 min with progress and follow up on any billing/credits." :white_check_mark:

kevin (acct-eng): Eve confirmed via DM: Greenridge will accept post-facto invoice. I'll capture the cost delta and propose a one-time credit if this was initiated by Redwood ops.

jordan (platform): follow-up mitigations: - set per-tenant soft concurrency limit to 40 to prevent single-tenant blast radius - enable eviction of pinned sessions older than 30m in dedicated pools (temporary policy) - recommend customer adopt scheduled job windowing + lower batch size. I'll open tickets for infra config changes.

anna (runtime): we've also pushed a temporary rule to deprioritize known non-interactive jobs for greenridge by routing them to hosted best-effort queue (they won't be front-page critical). Implemented via: 
```
routingctl set-priority --tenant greenridge --rule "job_type==batch" --priority low
```

lee (sre): metrics at 3178882700: queue_depth 12, 429 rate 0.6%, median p50 latency 250ms, p95 1.8s. Looks healthy. Recommend we keep burst active for 20m to let backlog clear then scale down to baseline.

sarah (on-call): agreed. We'll keep incident open until everything stable and customer notified. Handoff plan: I'm going to bed in ~30m; Jordan will be primary on-call for follow-up escalation. Jordan, can you accept?

jordan (platform): accepted. I'll watch the alerts and coordinate the rollback of burst once backlog clears. I'll also ensure the infra tickets for soft-limits and eviction policy are prioritized.

eve (greenridge-liaison): thanks team — product is noticing steady recovery. Appreciate quick response.

beth (cs): CS update sent to customers affected with an ETA note and link to support ticket.

lee (sre): planned rollback steps: 
1) verify queue_depth < 10 and 429s < 0.5% for 10m
2) run: `redwoodctl pools burst --pool greenridge-prod-pool --remove-gpus 8 --reason "rollback after backlog clear"`
3) monitor for re-spike 15m post-rollback.

anna (runtime): added temporary eviction policy config: `evict_pinned_sessions_after: 30m` (applied to greenridge-prod-pool). Will revert in the config PR.

sarah (on-call): closing notes: root cause: unplanned customer batch job + pinned long-lived sessions exhausted single-tenant dedicated pool that had bursting disabled. Mitigation: enabled emergency burst (+8 GPUs), deprioritized batch jobs, evicted old pinned sessions, and set temporary concurrency/eviction safeguards. Owners: anna (burst + runtime changes), lee (monitoring/rollback), jordan (platform follow-ups), kevin (billing), beth (cs comms). Handoff to jordan as primary. Will update incident ticket with timeline.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated at 3178883320, severity:high -> reduced. Please file post-incident review if any config changes persist beyond 72h.

jordan (platform): acknowledged handoff, will run rollback when stable and open follow-up PRs for: - soft tenant concurrency limits - eviction defaults - burst policy docs.

beth (cs): logging support ticket IDs: #GR-34521, #GR-34522. Will attach notes and customer confirmation.

eve (greenridge-liaison): thanks all. We'll coordinate with our ops to reschedule that nightly job.

sarah (on-call): handing off and setting a reminder to check after rollback. Good job team. :raised_hands:
